skill.name: cellxgene-census
skill.description: Query and analyze CZ CELLxGENE Census data with practical guidance for metadata filters, expression matrices, out-of-core workflows, PyTorch training, and Scanpy integration.
skill.summary: Query CZ CELLxGENE Census data for single-cell genomics research.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

content.value_statement: Single-cell Census queries can be hard to scope, filter, and load efficiently. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through reliable CELLxGENE Census workflows.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to open stable or versioned Census releases with context managers.
Builds obs and var filters for tissues, diseases, cell types, organisms, and genes.
Explains when to use get_obs, get_var, get_anndata, axis_query, and experiment_dataloader.
Guides large-query planning with metadata checks and out-of-core batch processing.
Documents common metadata fields, filter syntax, duplicate-cell handling, and versioning practices.
limitations: Requires the CELLxGENE Census Python package and access to the Census data service.
Does not analyze private datasets directly; use Scanpy or scvi-tools for local data.
Large expression queries still depend on available memory, storage, and compute resources.
Examples may need updates when Census releases or experimental APIs change.

use_cases.title: Explore cell populations
use_cases.description: Find available cell types, tissues, diseases, and donor metadata before loading expression matrices.

use_cases.title: Build reference datasets
use_cases.description: Create focused AnnData objects for marker genes, tissues, diseases, or cross-dataset comparisons.

use_cases.title: Train Census-based models
use_cases.description: Plan PyTorch dataloaders and train-test splits for large single-cell learning tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Explore a tissue
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the cellxgene-census skill to list available human lung cell types. Include the primary-data filter and needed columns.

prompt_templates.title: Query marker genes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the cellxgene-census skill to plan an AnnData query for CD4, CD8A, and CD19 in human T and B cells.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a large query
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the cellxgene-census skill to design an out-of-core brain tissue query and explain how to estimate query size first.

prompt_templates.title: Design model training
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the cellxgene-census skill to outline a PyTorch workflow for training a cell type classifier from Census data.

output_examples.input: Find immune cell types in human lung without loading expression data.
output_examples.output: The response gives a metadata-only query plan, required columns, a primary-data filter, and a count-by-cell-type summary approach.

output_examples.input: Compare marker gene expression across lung, liver, and kidney macrophages.
output_examples.output: The response recommends a focused gene filter, tissue filter, Census version pinning, and Scanpy-ready AnnData handling.

output_examples.input: Train a model on all primary human Census cells.
output_examples.output: The response recommends a dataloader-based workflow, batch processing, label selection, validation splits, and resource checks.

best_practices: Always include is_primary_data when duplicate cells would bias the analysis.
Pin a Census version when results must be reproducible.
Use metadata queries to estimate size before loading expression matrices.
anti_patterns: Loading broad expression matrices before checking available cell counts.
Mixing Census versions within one analysis without documenting the difference.
Querying marker genes without checking dataset presence or gene identifiers.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps design reliable queries against CZ CELLxGENE Census data and related analysis workflows.

faq.question: Does it download Census data by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for using the CELLxGENE Census Python API.

faq.question: Can it help with very large queries?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains metadata size checks and out-of-core processing with axis queries.

faq.question: Can I use it with Scanpy?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for creating AnnData objects and applying Scanpy workflows.

faq.question: Can it support machine learning workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers the experimental PyTorch dataloader and train-test split patterns.

faq.question: Should I use it for my own private data?
faq.answer: No. Use Scanpy, scvi-tools, or local pipelines for private datasets outside the Census.
